methodology.record_note: CANTO predicts the complete native AhmedML surface and volume fields from the NURBS description of the body. The geometry input is a 13-patch, 72-control-point NURBS net plus its level-4 subdivided anchor net; the native meshes supply cell-centroid positions only, as query points and as volume anchor positions, and never field data. Predictions come from actual inference with the single checkpoint declared below, decoded at every native cell in source order, so no interpolation or mapping is applied before scoring. The model was trained from scratch on 399 AhmedML cases, none of them among the 50 Full test cases (run_500 was not used), and monitored on 50 further validation cases. The declared checkpoint, model.pt, is the last checkpoint written by the single training run, at optimizer step 86000 of a 100000-step cosine schedule: the tenth four-hour training job reached its time limit after writing it, and the run was not resubmitted because the validation loss had plateaued. Contact with the public test cases: the training configuration enabled test-split evaluation, so test-split metrics were computed and logged alongside the validation metrics every ten epochs. Before this package was assembled, the run's validation-selected checkpoint (model_best.pt, tracked on validation surface-pressure relative L2) was also run on the same 50 test cases and scored with the candidate evaluator; that result is not submitted. The submitter states that submitting the final checkpoint was decided before any test-split score was seen, that test-split metrics did not influence training, stopping or checkpoint selection, and that every normalisation statistic was computed from training cases only.

architecture.description: Two-stage model. A Perceiver-style NURBS geometry encoder pools the control net of each patch into latent tokens using bucketed variable-length attention over control points together with learned embeddings of the two knot vectors, then refines those tokens with latent self-attention. An anchored branched transformer (AB-UPT) conditions on the resulting geometry tokens: a shared trunk is followed by separate surface and volume branches, each of which first predicts at a set of anchor positions and then lets arbitrary query points attend to those anchors. Surface anchors are patch centroids of a subdivided NURBS net and volume anchors are native volume cell centroids drawn from the query set. Query points are never attention keys, so any number of them can be decoded in chunks without changing the result. Control points and query coordinates share one union min/max normalisation frame.

components.description: Bucketed variable-length Perceiver pool over NURBS control points with separate u and v knot-vector encoders, followed by six latent self-attention blocks. Produces the geometry token set consumed by every downstream branch.
Shared AB-UPT trunk applied to geometry tokens before the surface and volume branches diverge.
Anchored surface branch. Predicts at NURBS patch-centroid anchors, then decodes arbitrary surface query points by attention to those anchors.
Anchored volume branch. Predicts at sampled volume anchors, then decodes arbitrary volume query points by attention to those anchors.

key_hyperparameters.name: token width and head count
key_hyperparameters.description: Width of the AB-UPT trunk and both branches.

key_hyperparameters.name: block pattern and branch depth
key_hyperparameters.description: Interleaving of pooling, self-attention and cross-attention blocks in the trunk, and the number of blocks in each branch.

key_hyperparameters.name: geometry latent depth
key_hyperparameters.description: Latent self-attention blocks applied to geometry tokens after pooling.

key_hyperparameters.name: Perceiver pool configuration
key_hyperparameters.value: 8 latents, hidden 128, 4 heads, depth 4, positional encoding 64, knot depth 1, self-attention on, variable-length on, ReZero off
key_hyperparameters.description: Per-patch pooling of the control net into latent tokens.

key_hyperparameters.name: anchor and query counts
key_hyperparameters.value: 3328 surface anchors (one per patch of the level-4 subdivided NURBS net), 16384 volume anchors, 16384 surface and 16384 volume queries per training step
key_hyperparameters.description: Training draws new surface queries, volume anchors and volume queries at every step. Inference draws the volume anchors once per case and decodes every native cell, in chunks of 2000000 queries.

key_hyperparameters.name: surface anchor dropout
key_hyperparameters.description: Fraction of surface anchor tokens dropped at random at each training step. Inference keeps every anchor.

key_hyperparameters.name: shared control-point and query coordinate frame
key_hyperparameters.value: enabled, bounds taken from query-coordinate statistics
key_hyperparameters.description: Control points and query coordinates are normalised in one union min/max frame. The loaded statistics carry no control-point bounds, so the documented fallback to query-coordinate bounds is used, matching the code path the run trained under.

input_features.name: NURBS control net
input_features.description: Homogeneous control points (x, y, z, w) of the 13 NURBS patches describing the body. 72 control points per case. This is the complete geometry input; no native mesh entity is read as geometry.

input_features.name: knot vectors
input_features.description: Per-patch u and v knot vectors, encoded by dedicated knot pooling modules.

input_features.name: subdivided NURBS patch centroids
input_features.description: Anchor positions derived from a level-4 subdivision of the same NURBS description, not sampled from the native mesh.

input_features.name: native cell centroid coordinates
input_features.description: Cell-centroid coordinates of the native surface and volume meshes, used as query positions and, for 16384 volume cells per case, as volume anchor positions. No native field value is read at inference time.

predicted_fields.description: Direct surface branch output channel, denormalised to the dataset's kinematic pressure units. One value per native surface cell.
Direct surface branch output channels, denormalised to the dataset's units. Three components per native surface cell.
Direct volume branch output channels, denormalised to the dataset's units. Three components per native volume cell.
Direct volume branch output channel, denormalised to the dataset's kinematic pressure units. One value per native volume cell.

data_handling.normalization: Surface output channels are standardised by the per-channel mean and standard deviation stored in surface_flow_stats.pt, and volume output channels by those stored in volume_flow_stats_with_cpt.pt. These files, the coordinate statistics in volume_coords_stats.pt and the NURBS input statistics in inputs_NURBS_stats.pt were all computed from training cases only. Control points and query coordinates share one union min/max frame; the loaded input statistics carry mean and standard deviation but no control-point bounds, so the frame falls back to the query-coordinate bounds in volume_coords_stats.pt, which is the code path the checkpoint was trained under. Predictions are denormalised to physical units before being written, so the evaluator receives raw dataset units.
data_handling.preprocessing: Training reads HDF5 shards converted once from the public VTP and VTU files, carrying cell-centroid coordinates, cell areas, surface normals and field values; the volume shards hold every native volume cell in shuffled order. Inference therefore takes its query positions straight from the published VTP and VTU files, recomputing each native cell centroid by averaging the cell's vertices, which matches how the training coordinates were produced and handles the polyhedral volume cells. Geometry and anchor nets come from the NURBS archives. No remeshing, decimation or smoothing is applied at any stage.
data_handling.sampling: Training draws 16384 surface queries, 16384 volume anchors and 16384 volume queries per geometry at every step, uniformly from the case's native cells, and drops 10 percent of the surface anchors. Inference does not subsample the outputs: every native surface and volume cell is decoded exactly once in source order, in chunks of 2000000 queries, each against the same geometry and anchor context. The 16384 volume anchor positions are drawn once per case from the native volume centroids, from a random generator seeded with 0 at the start of each of the four inference worker processes, which take the cases round-robin in run-number order.

stages.description: Single joint stage training all components end to end from random initialisation on 399 AhmedML training cases, with 50 validation cases monitored every ten epochs. No pretraining and no staged freezing.

loss.description: Mean squared error between standardised predictions and targets at the sampled surface and volume query points. The surface target has four channels (pressure and three wall-shear-stress components); the volume target has eight (pressure, three velocity components, three vorticity components and the total-pressure coefficient), of which vorticity and total-pressure coefficient are auxiliary outputs that are not submitted.
loss.weighting: Surface loss plus 0.2 times volume loss; all channels within each term carry equal weight.

optimizers.name: Lion
optimizers.schedule: Linear warmup over 1000 steps, then cosine annealing to 1e-6 over a 100000-step horizon. Betas (0.9, 0.99), weight decay 0.05, gradient-norm clipping at 1.0, full fp32 precision.

compute.hardware: NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, eight GPUs on one node per job
compute.measurement_notes: One training run executed as ten consecutive single-node jobs of eight GPUs, each resuming from the previous rolling checkpoint and ending at its four-hour time limit; the experiment tracker recorded eight NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 devices for every job. Elapsed campaign time runs from the first job's start (2026-09-08T13:24Z) to the last job's end (about 2026-09-10T06:33Z), about 41.2 hours, including queue gaps of a few minutes between most jobs and about one hour between the sixth and seventh, during which no devices were held. Aggregate device time sums the actual allocations, ten jobs of four hours on eight GPUs, which is 320 GPU-hours; the tracker's cumulative process runtime is 39.8 hours, about 319 GPU-hours. Both include job start-up, dependency installation, checkpoint input and output, and the validation and test-split monitoring evaluations every ten epochs. The last job trained about 150 steps past the declared step-86000 checkpoint before its time limit; that work is included. Earlier exploratory runs and hyperparameter search are not counted.

checkpoints.bytes_description: The exact 51507803-byte PyTorch checkpoint file (model.pt) loaded for every case in this submission, containing the state dictionary of all four components of the single joint model. It is byte-identical to the run's rolling step-86000 checkpoint.
checkpoints.selection_rule: The last checkpoint written by the single training run (model.pt, optimizer step 86000), not the run's validation-selected checkpoint (model_best.pt). The rule to submit the final checkpoint was fixed before any test-split score was seen, and the run was not resubmitted after its tenth job because the validation loss had plateaued.

inference_compute.hardware: NVIDIA GB200, four GPUs on one node
inference_compute.measurement_notes: One scheduler job on one node with four GPUs; the fifty cases were dealt round-robin to four worker processes, one per GPU. Wall time is the job's elapsed time and includes container dependency installation, checkpoint and geometry loading, and writing about 25 GB of prediction chunks to shared storage, so it overstates pure forward-pass cost. Aggregate device time is wall time multiplied by the four allocated GPUs, idle time included. Mapping is the identity because every native cell is decoded directly, so no separate mapping cost exists. Native cell-centroid extraction from the published VTP and VTU files ran earlier as a separate CPU job and is excluded. The export job did not log device names; the GPU model is reported by the submitter, and a job on the same partition that day recorded four NVIDIA GB200 devices.

evaluation.command: Inference: export_ahmedml_native_predictions.py --checkpoint final --seed 0 --rows-per-chunk 1000000 --query-chunk 2000000 (four workers, one GPU each). Evaluation: python scripts/ahmedml.py evaluate-entry my-entry --dataset-root <ahmedml-dataset-root> --support-root support/ahmedml --output work/canto-full --resume --offline. Packaging: python scripts/ahmedml.py package --evaluation-root work/canto-full/evaluation --config my-entry/package-config.json --discretization-cases my-entry/discretization-cases.jsonl --checkpoint canto-joint-model=model.pt --output submissions/ahmedml/ahmedml-canto-full-v1
